content: Infection caused by Streptococcus pneumoniae is a significant contributor to pneumonia and other severe illnesses, especially in individuals with certain high-risk medical conditions, such as asthma. Although the pneumococcal vaccine is commonly recommended for individuals with asthma, there is uncertainty regarding the strength of the evidence supporting this recommendation. The objective of this study was to evaluate the effectiveness of the pneumococcal vaccine in reducing mortality or morbidity associated with pneumococcal disease in individuals with asthma. To achieve this, randomized controlled trials (RCTs) were identified through the Cochrane Airways Group Specialised Register of trials, with searches updated as of August 2010. The inclusion criteria for the study required RCTs, either blinded or unblinded, that compared the pneumococcal vaccine with a placebo or no treatment in individuals with asthma diagnosed by a clinician. Two independent reviewers assessed all abstracts and retrieved full-text articles deemed potentially relevant. The methodological quality of the studies was evaluated using the Cochrane approach and the Jadad rating scale. Data extraction was performed by one reviewer and independently verified by a second reviewer. Quantitative analyses of outcomes were planned on an intention-to-treat basis, where feasible. Out of the three studies initially retrieved, only one met the inclusion criteria. However, the methodological quality of this study was poor, as it was unblinded and lacked adequate allocation concealment. Due to the limited data, no meta-analysis could be performed. In a subset of 30 asthmatic children who were prone to recurrent episodes of otitis media, pneumococcal vaccination was shown to reduce the incidence of acute asthma exacerbations from 10 episodes to 7 episodes per child per year. A subsequent search conducted in August 2010 did not identify any additional studies. The authors concluded that there is very limited evidence to support the routine use of the pneumococcal vaccine in individuals with asthma. They emphasized the need for a well-designed randomized controlled trial to evaluate the efficacy of the vaccine in both children and adults with asthma.
